description: Enriched story ideas organized by reading level for the book creation wizard

A0.title: Look!
A0.concept: A wordless or near-wordless book showing a child discovering things around them. Each page reveals something new to look at - a bug, a flower, a bird.
A0.character: Maya, a curious toddler with big brown eyes and springy curls
A0.setting: Backyard garden on a sunny morning
A0.story_arc: Maya explores the garden, finding one amazing thing after another, ending with sharing her discoveries with a parent
A0.visual_style: Soft watercolors, warm palette, close-up details of nature

A0.title: Big and Small
A0.concept: Visual comparison book exploring opposites through pairs: big elephant, small mouse. Big tree, small seed. Pictures carry all meaning with minimal text.
A0.story_arc: Each spread shows a big/small pair, ending with big and small friends playing together
A0.visual_style: Bold shapes, high contrast, playful compositions

A0.title: Hello, Friends!
A0.concept: A greeting book where a child waves hello to everyone they meet - the dog, the cat, the bird, their friend. Simple social interaction.
A0.character: Leo, a friendly boy who loves saying hi to everyone
A0.story_arc: Leo greets each friend, they wave back, ends with a group wave

A1.title: I Am Sam
A1.concept: Simple self-introduction labels: 'I am Sam.' Sam shows what he can do - sit, run, hop. One action per page with supporting illustration.
A1.character: Sam, a spotted puppy with floppy ears and boundless energy
A1.story_arc: Sam introduces himself, shows his tricks, ends with 'I am Sam. I am happy!'
A1.visual_style: Clean lines, minimal backgrounds, focus on character action

A1.title: The Cat Sat
A1.concept: A cat finds different places to sit: on a mat, on a hat, in a pan. Repetitive structure with one changing word per page.
A1.character: Whiskers, a round orange tabby who loves finding cozy spots
A1.story_arc: Cat tries many spots, none quite right, finally finds the perfect lap
A1.visual_style: Warm interior scenes, soft textures, cozy feeling

A1.title: Tap, Tap, Tap
A1.concept: A little bird taps on things to make sounds: tap on a can, tap on a pan, tap on a hat! Playful sound exploration.
A1.character: Pip, a tiny woodpecker learning to peck
A1.story_arc: Pip taps everything, makes silly sounds, finds the perfect tree
A1.visual_style: Energetic, action lines, fun sound effect visuals

A2.title: I See the ___
A2.concept: Repetitive frame: 'I see the cat.' 'I see the mat.' Only one word changes each page. Child narrator points out things on a walk.
A2.character: Emma, an observant girl with glasses and a red jacket
A2.story_arc: Emma notices small details others miss, shares them with reader
A2.visual_style: Detailed backgrounds with highlighted objects, nature illustrations

A2.title: The Pig Did Sit
A2.concept: Pattern book: 'The pig did sit.' 'The pig did dig.' Same sentence frame, changing action verb. Playful farm pig antics.
A2.character: Gus, a cheerful pink pig who can't sit still
A2.story_arc: Pig tries to sit but keeps finding fun things to do, finally rests at sunset
A2.visual_style: Expressive character, muddy textures, warm farm colors

A2.title: Mom and Me
A2.concept: Simple activity book: 'Mom and me hop.' 'Mom and me run.' Showing parent-child activities together.
A2.character: A bunny kit and their mom
A2.story_arc: Activities through the day, ending with bedtime snuggle
A2.visual_style: Gentle, soft colors, tender moments captured

A3.title: The Cat Is Here
A3.concept: Simple declaratives with slight variation. 'The cat is here. The cat is on it. The cat ran fast!' Cat explores and gets into mischief.
A3.character: Mittens, a curious gray kitten with white paws
A3.setting: Living room with furniture to climb
A3.story_arc: Cat explores room, causes minor chaos, gets caught, forgiven with cuddles
A3.visual_style: Dynamic poses, domestic setting, humor in expressions

A3.title: Where Is Pup?
A3.concept: Hide and seek story. 'Is Pup in the box? No! Is Pup on the bed? No!' Building to a fun reveal.
A3.character: Pup, a small brown dachshund who loves hiding
A3.story_arc: Reader searches with narrator, finds Pup in unexpected place
A3.visual_style: Interactive feel, search-and-find elements, cozy room

A3.title: Run, Bug, Run!
A3.concept: Action chase story. 'The bug ran. The frog ran. Run, bug, run!' Simple excitement and movement.
A3.character: A tiny ladybug being chased by friendly animals
A3.story_arc: Bug flees various creatures, finds safe home in a flower
A3.visual_style: Bug's-eye view, oversized plants, dramatic angles

A4.title: Sam and the Hat
A4.concept: Bridge to narrative. Sam finds a hat, tries it on, it's too big! He tries to give it away but everyone says no. Finally finds the perfect owner.
A4.character: Sam, a helpful puppy who finds a fancy top hat
A4.story_arc: Problem (big hat) → attempts to solve → satisfying resolution
A4.visual_style: Expressive character emotions, the hat as visual comedy

A4.title: The Lost Sock
A4.concept: Mini-mystery: Where did the sock go? Child searches high and low, silly places, finally finds it somewhere unexpected.
A4.character: Ben, a boy getting dressed who's missing one sock
A4.setting: Bedroom becoming increasingly messy during search
A4.visual_style: Progressively messier room, humor in the chaos

A4.title: Hop to the Top
A4.concept: Frog wants to see the view from the top of the hill. Hops and hops, gets tired, almost gives up, makes it! Beautiful view.
A4.character: Fritz, a determined little green frog
A4.visual_style: Vertical composition showing height, triumphant final spread

B1.title: The Big Pig
B1.concept: Tim has a big pig who gets too hot in the sun. Tim digs a pit, but pig won't go in. Tim has to get creative with jam and bags to coax pig into the cool pit.
B1.character: Tim, a resourceful farm boy, and his stubborn but lovable pink pig
B1.setting: Sunny farm with barn and pigpen
B1.story_arc: Problem (hot pig) → failed solution → creative solution → success
B1.visual_style: Warm farm colors, expressive pig emotions, summer heat feeling

B1.title: Pip Gets a Hit
B1.concept: Pip the pig wants to play baseball but keeps missing. Friends encourage her. Finally connects - a big hit! Team celebrates.
B1.character: Pip, a small pig with a big baseball dream, and her supportive animal friends
B1.setting: Sunny baseball diamond at the park
B1.visual_style: Sporty, dynamic action poses, team spirit feeling

B1.title: Dan's Big Van
B1.concept: Dan the ram has a van. He picks up friends one by one for an adventure. Van gets full! Where are they going? A surprise picnic!
B1.character: Dan, a friendly ram with a colorful van, various animal passengers
B1.setting: Country road leading to a meadow
B1.story_arc: Picking up friends → journey → surprise destination → shared joy
B1.visual_style: Cheerful, the van as a character, progressively fuller scenes

B1.title: The Sad Lad
B1.concept: Chad is sad. He lost his cap. Friends help him look - not in the bag, not on the cat. Dad finds it! Chad is glad.
B1.character: Chad, a young boy, and his helpful dad and pet cat
B1.story_arc: Loss → sadness → search with help → found → happiness
B1.visual_style: Expressive emotions, cozy home setting, warm resolution

B2.title: Pup in the Mud
B2.concept: Max the puppy sees a mud puddle. Should he? He shouldn't... but he does! SPLASH! So much fun! Then Mom sees him. Bath time!
B2.character: Max, an energetic golden puppy who can't resist mud
B2.story_arc: Temptation → giving in → pure joy → cleanup → still worth it
B2.visual_style: Dynamic mud splashes, expressive dog joy, sudsy bath contrast

B2.title: Frog Gets Fun
B2.concept: Fred the frog is bored on his log. Tries hopping - not fun enough. Tries swimming - still bored. Discovers he can make music by croaking with friends!
B2.character: Fred, a contemplative green frog seeking excitement
B2.visual_style: Peaceful pond setting, musical notes visual, frog expressions

B2.title: The Red Hen
B2.concept: Hen wants to make bread. 'Who will help?' Not cat. Not dog. Not pig. Hen does it herself. When bread is ready - who wants some? She shares anyway.
B2.character: Red Hen, hardworking and kind; lazy but lovable farm friends
B2.story_arc: Task → repeated refusals → solo effort → surprising generosity
B2.visual_style: Classic farm tale, warm kitchen scenes, character expressions

B2.title: Hot Dog
B2.concept: It's a hot day. Dog pants. Dog digs. Dog finds shade. But then - the sprinkler turns on! Best day ever!
B2.character: Buster, a shaggy dog trying to cool off
B2.story_arc: Problem → attempts → bigger problem → unexpected solution → joy
B2.visual_style: Summer heat visuals, water spray joy, dog expressions

B2.title: The Bug Hut
B2.concept: Gus the bug needs a home. Tries a cup - too dark. Tries a nut - too small. Builds his own hut from a leaf. Perfect!
B2.story_arc: Need → failed options → creative building → satisfaction
B2.visual_style: Tiny world perspective, leaf architecture, cozy ending

B3.title: Jump at Camp
B3.concept: Animal friends at summer camp compete in silly events: who can jump highest? Stomp loudest? By the campfire, they realize everyone won something.
B3.character: Rabbit, Bear, Frog, and Mouse - camp friends with different strengths
B3.story_arc: Competition → various events → no clear winner → realization → celebration
B3.visual_style: Camp activities, woodland setting, medal/ribbon imagery

B3.title: Rex and the Runaway Ball
B3.concept: Rex's ball rolls away - down the hill, past the pond, into the wind! He chases it through obstacles, finally catching it just before it goes too far.
B3.character: Rex, a determined fox with a favorite red ball
B3.story_arc: Loss → chase → obstacles → near misses → triumphant catch
B3.visual_style: Dynamic movement, ball as red focal point, landscape variety

B3.title: The Best Nest
B3.concept: Bird wants to build the perfect nest. Tries stiff sticks - too poky. Tries soft fluff - flies away! Combines both for the best nest on the hill.
B3.character: Wren, a perfectionist bird preparing for eggs
phonics_focus: FLOSS rule: ff, ll, ss, zz
B3.story_arc: Goal → failed extremes → combination solution → success
B3.visual_style: Nest-building details, forest textures, cozy final nest

B3.title: Lost and Found
B3.concept: Jill loses her doll at the mall. Asks for help - the man at the desk, the lady with the cart. Finally found in the lost and found!
B3.character: Jill, a young girl, and helpful mall workers
B3.story_arc: Loss → worry → asking for help → helpers → reunion
B3.visual_style: Mall setting, emotional journey, happy reunion

B4.title: Frog and Crab
B4.concept: Frog lives by the pond, Crab lives by the sea. They meet at the stream and become unlikely friends. They swim, skip, and grab snacks together.
phonics_focus: Initial blends: fr-, cr-, gr-, sw-, sk-
B4.story_arc: Meeting → initial confusion → finding common ground → friendship
B4.visual_style: Two ecosystems blending, playful interaction poses

B4.title: Flicker the Firefly
B4.concept: Flicker can't make her light work. Other fireflies glow brightly. She tries and tries - nothing. Then one dark night, a lost baby rabbit needs help. Flicker tries so hard... she glows!
B4.character: Flicker, a young firefly who's a late bloomer
phonics_focus: Initial blends: fl-, gl-, br-, tr-
B4.theme: Finding your light when others need you
B4.story_arc: Struggle → comparison → crisis → rising to occasion → triumph
B4.visual_style: Dark backgrounds, glowing effects, emotional lighting

B4.title: The Sled Run
B4.concept: First snow! Friends grab sleds and race down the hill. Slip, slide, spin! Someone crashes - are they okay? Yes, laughing! Best snow day ever.
B4.character: Group of animal friends (Bear, Rabbit, Fox, Squirrel)
B4.story_arc: Excitement → racing → crash → checking on friend → relief → more fun
B4.visual_style: White snow, colorful scarves, action and movement

B4.title: Drip, Drop, Plop
B4.concept: Rain starts slowly - drip. Then faster - drop. Then a downpour - PLOP! Animals find shelter, then splash in puddles when it stops.
B4.character: Various forest animals seeking shelter together
B4.theme: Finding joy in weather, community shelter
B4.story_arc: Rain begins → seeking shelter → togetherness → rain stops → puddle joy
B4.visual_style: Rain effects, cozy shelter, splashing action

B5.title: The Ship in the Shell
B5.concept: Child finds a shell on the beach. Holds it to ear - hears the ocean... and a tiny ship! Imagines sailing away to adventure, then puts shell back for the next dreamer.
B5.character: Shelly, a imaginative girl with a found shell
B5.story_arc: Discovery → imagination journey → return → passing it on
B5.visual_style: Realistic beach to fantasy sea, shell as portal, dreamy colors

B5.title: Zip the Little Snail
B5.concept: Zip the snail wishes he could dash like the rabbit, swoosh like the fish. He feels too slow. But when a friend needs patient help, Zip's slowness saves the day.
B5.character: Zip, a philosophical snail who dreams of speed
B5.theme: Embracing who you are, slow and steady
B5.story_arc: Wishing to be different → failed attempts → crisis → slow saves day → self-acceptance
B5.visual_style: Speed lines for others, detailed slow journey, triumphant ending

B5.title: The Shell Switch
B5.concept: Hermit crab needs a new shell. Tries this one, that one - too big, too small, too fancy. Has to trade and negotiate. Finds just right one with a friend's help.
B5.character: Chester the hermit crab and tide pool friends
B5.theme: Finding where you fit, helping others
B5.story_arc: Need → search → rejections → friend helps → perfect fit
B5.visual_style: Underwater detail, various shell designs, community feeling

B5.title: The Path to the Thatch
B5.concept: Three chicks must find their way home before dark. Follow the path, cross the bridge, through the thick brush to the thatch-roof barn. They make it!
B5.character: Three brave chicks on a journey
B5.story_arc: Separation → journey with obstacles → teamwork → home safe
B5.visual_style: Journey map feeling, increasing darkness, warm home at end

B6.title: Kate and the Lake
B6.concept: Kate wants to swim in the lake but is scared. She wades in slowly, goes deeper each day. Finally swims all the way to the raft! Pride in overcoming fear.
B6.character: Kate, a cautious girl who conquers her fear of deep water
B6.setting: Summer lake with dock and swimming raft
B6.story_arc: Fear → small steps → progress → setback → triumph
B6.visual_style: Lake scenes, emotional progression, triumphant swim

B6.title: Bake Day
B6.concept: Animals prepare for the village bake sale. Each makes something special - cake, dates, grapes. When oven breaks, they combine efforts to bake one amazing creation!
B6.story_arc: Individual efforts → crisis → teamwork → combined success → celebration
B6.visual_style: Warm kitchen, baking details, community celebration

B6.title: The Bike Ride
B6.concept: Mike gets a new bike but can't ride yet. Falls, tries, falls again. Big sister Jane helps. Finally rides alone - down the whole street! Freedom feeling.
B6.character: Mike, a determined boy, and Jane, his patient sister
B6.visual_style: Learning progression, balance attempts, joyful riding

B6.title: Home Sweet Home
B6.concept: Mole digs a new home. Needs to be just right - not too close to the stone, not under the rose. Finds the perfect spot and invites friends to see.
B6.character: Mole, a particular digger who knows what he wants
B6.theme: Creating a home, knowing what you need
B6.story_arc: Search → rejecting wrong spots → finding perfect spot → creating home → sharing
B6.visual_style: Cross-section underground views, cozy burrow details

B7.title: A Day at the Farm
B7.concept: Follow the farmer through the day - feeding the goats, milking, collecting eggs. Each task with rain threatening. Storm comes, but all animals are safe in the barn!
B7.character: Farmer Mae and her various farm animals
B7.story_arc: Morning tasks → weather watching → racing storm → safe in barn
B7.visual_style: Farm life details, darkening sky progression, cozy barn ending

B7.title: The Rain and the Snow
B7.concept: Two weather fairies - Rain and Snow - argue about who should visit today. They compromise: rain in the morning, snow in the afternoon. Everyone's happy!
B7.character: Rain (cheerful, wet) and Snow (sparkly, cold) as fairy characters
phonics_focus: Vowel teams: ai, ay, oa, ow
B7.story_arc: Conflict → argument → compromise idea → execution → harmony
B7.visual_style: Weather personified, village scenes, both weather beauties shown

B7.title: Sail Away
B7.concept: A toy boat (made by a child) sails down the stream, having adventures: passing ducks, going through the drain, reaching the bay. Bittersweet letting go.
B7.character: The toy boat as protagonist, child who made it at bookends
B7.theme: Letting go and trusting the journey
B7.story_arc: Creation → launch → journey → near-dangers → reaching the sea
B7.visual_style: Water journey, boat's perspective, landscape changing

B7.title: The Dream Team
B7.concept: Group of animals have different dreams - Bee wants to see the sea, Sheep wants to sleep on a cloud, Seal wants to feel the forest. They help each other's dreams come true.
B7.character: Bee, Sheep, and Seal - dreamers who help each other
B7.story_arc: Dreams shared → planning → helping each other → dreams achieved
B7.visual_style: Dreamy quality, each dream vignette, friendship warmth

B8.title: The Day the Rain Came
B8.concept: Owl, Cow, and Mouse were going to have a picnic. Rain came! They found shelter in a house by the brook. Made the best indoor picnic instead.
B8.character: Owl (wise), Cow (practical), Mouse (cheerful) - different reactions to rain
B8.theme: Making the best of changed plans
B8.story_arc: Plans → rain ruins plans → disappointment → adaptation → joy anyway
B8.visual_style: Outdoor to indoor transition, cozy cottage details

B8.title: The Owl and the Mouse
B8.concept: Owl and Mouse seem like they shouldn't be friends (owl might eat mouse!). But they bond over shared love of the night. Trust builds slowly into friendship.
B8.character: Oliver Owl and Millie Mouse - unlikely friends
B8.story_arc: Fear/distrust → small kindness → more kindness → trust → friendship
B8.visual_style: Nighttime atmosphere, size contrast played for emotion

B8.title: The Cloud House
B8.concept: A girl looks at clouds and imagines living in a cloud house. Room by room she decorates it in her mind - fluffy beds, rainbow windows. Then rain falls - her house melts! But tomorrow, new clouds, new house.
B8.character: Luna, a dreamer who looks up
B8.setting: Backyard looking at sky, then imagination sequences
B8.theme: Imagination is renewable, impermanence is okay
B8.story_arc: Dreaming → building in mind → enjoying → loss → acceptance → new beginning
B8.visual_style: Realistic to dreamy transitions, cloud architecture

B8.title: Too Loud!
B8.concept: New neighbors move in - they're SO LOUD! Banging, shouting, noise noise noise! Turns out they're building a playground for the whole neighborhood. Worth it!
B8.character: Grumpy Groundhog annoyed by new neighbors (Woodpecker family)
B8.theme: Patience, jumping to conclusions, community benefit
B8.visual_style: Noise visualized, before/after neighborhood, happy ending

B9.title: A Star at the Farm
B9.concept: After a big storm, Emma goes to the barn to check on her horse, Star. Star is scared but Emma stays calm. Together they watch the storm end and the real stars come out.
B9.character: Emma, a brave farm girl, and Star, her anxious horse
B9.setting: Farm during and after storm, nighttime
B9.theme: Being calm for those who need you, mutual comfort
B9.story_arc: Storm fear → going to help → calming Star → storm passes → beauty emerges
B9.visual_style: Storm drama, barn warmth, starry sky resolution

B9.title: The Owl and the Boy
B9.concept: A boy can't sleep. Goes to his window, sees an owl. They have a silent conversation through the night. Owl shows boy the farm, the forest, the stars. Boy finally sleeps, at peace.
B9.character: Marcus, an insomniac boy, and a wise old owl
phonics_focus: R-controlled: all patterns - ar, or, er, ir, ur
B9.story_arc: Can't sleep → connection with owl → night journey → return → peaceful sleep
B9.visual_style: Nighttime blue palette, flying sequences, peaceful ending

B9.title: Purple Turtle's Thursday
B9.concept: Follow Purple Turtle through her day - morning at the fern, afternoon learning, evening returning home. Everyday magic in ordinary moments.
B9.character: Purple Turtle, a thoughtful reptile who appreciates life
B9.setting: Pond and forest through the day
B9.story_arc: Morning → midday → afternoon → evening - each part meaningful
B9.visual_style: Time-of-day lighting, peaceful scenes, nature details

B9.title: The Bird Who Hurt Her Wing
B9.concept: Bird hurts her wing and can't fly. Girl finds her, makes a perch, brings water and worms. Bird heals over days. Finally flies - returns one more time to say thanks.
B9.character: Vera (girl) and a injured sparrow she nurses back
B9.story_arc: Discovery → care → healing → release → bittersweet farewell
B9.visual_style: Tender care scenes, healing progress, triumphant flight

C1.title: The Knight's Quest
C1.concept: A knight must solve riddles to save the kingdom - each riddle involves silent letters. 'What has a KNEE but cannot bend? A KNIGHT in the garden!'
C1.character: Sir Cedric, a thinking knight who solves puzzles not fights
C1.story_arc: Kingdom in trouble → quest begins → riddles solved → kingdom saved
C1.visual_style: Medieval illuminated manuscript style, puzzle elements

C1.title: The Night Writer
C1.concept: A girl can only write at night - her stories come alive in dreams. She writes about a knitting gnome, a whistling knight. Her journal becomes magical.
C1.story_arc: Discovers writing at night → stories come alive → shares magic
C1.visual_style: Dreamy nighttime blues, words becoming images

C1.title: The Lamb Who Couldn't Keep Calm
C1.concept: A jittery lamb needs to learn to be still for the sheep counting competition. Tries everything. Finally learns by watching a ladybug on his knee - slow and steady.
C1.character: Lambert, an anxious lamb who vibrates with energy
C1.story_arc: Can't be still → failed attempts → unlikely teacher → success
C1.visual_style: Bouncy energy to calm stillness progression

C2.title: The Magic City
C2.concept: A young magician's trick goes wrong - the entire city is now made of gingerbread! Must find the original spell page to reverse it. Race against time (before rain!).
C2.character: Ginger, apprentice magician who made a delicious mistake
C2.story_arc: Mistake → discovery of consequences → search for solution → close call → fixed

C2.title: The Giant's Garden
C2.concept: A gentle giant is lonely because everyone fears him. He creates a magnificent garden. Children are curious, then brave enough to visit. Giant shares his gentle heart.
C2.character: Gerard the Giant, shy and kind, and curious village children
C2.theme: Don't judge by appearance, sharing brings joy
C2.story_arc: Loneliness → creation → curiosity → brave visitor → friendship
C2.visual_style: Scale contrasts, magnificent garden details, friendship warmth

C2.title: The Circus Mice
C2.concept: A family of mice live under the circus stage. They create their own tiny circus, mirroring the big one. A girl discovers them and keeps their secret, becoming their audience of one.
C2.character: The Cinnamon family of circus mice
C2.setting: Circus - both big stage and tiny mouse version below
phonics_focus: Soft c: circus, mice, nice, dance
C2.theme: Art happens at every scale, secret joys
C2.story_arc: Daily life → mouse circus revealed → discovery by girl → secret friendship
C2.visual_style: Parallel big/small circus scenes, wonder and whimsy

C3.title: The Kitten in the Basket
C3.concept: A kitten hides in a picnic basket. Gets carried to the park without anyone knowing! Must find way home. Uses clues - follows the butter smell back to the kitchen.
C3.character: Whisper, a curious kitten who got more adventure than expected
C3.theme: Curiosity and its consequences, finding your way home
C3.story_arc: Hiding → accidentally transported → lost → clue finding → home
C3.visual_style: Kitten's perspective, journey map, happy reunion

C3.title: The Hidden Mitten
C3.concept: A girl's favorite mitten disappears. She searches the entire house systematically - under the pillow, in the puppet box. Dog had it hidden in his bed all along.
C3.character: Hannah and her sneaky but lovable dog Tucker
C3.story_arc: Loss → organized search → dead ends → discovery → laughter
C3.visual_style: Search-and-find feel, cozy home, comedic reveal

C3.title: The Perfect Picnic
C3.concept: Friends plan a picnic. Everything goes wrong - ants in the basket, rain and thunder, forgotten napkins. But they're together, and that's what matters.
C3.character: Group of woodland friends with different personalities
C3.story_arc: Planning → disasters → considering giving up → choosing joy → happy ending
C3.visual_style: Chaos and laughter, rain then rainbow, friendship warmth

C4.title: The Robot and the Pilot
C4.concept: A robot and a human pilot must work together when their spaceship has trouble. Robot is logical, pilot is emotional. Together they combine strengths to land safely.
C4.character: ROB-7 (analytical robot) and Captain Luna (intuitive pilot)
C4.story_arc: Crisis → disagreement → combination of approaches → success → respect
C4.visual_style: Sci-fi retro style, split-screen robot/human, teamwork visuals

C4.title: The Paper Airplane
C4.concept: A boy makes the perfect paper airplane. He throws it - it catches the wind and goes impossibly far. He chases it through the town, finally catching it at sunset by the ocean.
C4.character: Max, a patient folder who creates something special
C4.story_arc: Creating → launching → chase → near catches → final catch
C4.visual_style: Airplane as white focal point, town panorama, movement

C4.title: Tiger Lily's Secret
C4.concept: A flower (Tiger Lily) in the garden knows a secret - there's treasure buried underneath. She hints to a little girl through movements. Together they dig and find a time capsule.
C4.character: Tiger Lily (the flower) and Sophia (the gardener's granddaughter)
C4.story_arc: Noticing hints → following clues → digging → discovery → understanding the past
C4.visual_style: Garden beauty, treasure hunt feel, vintage items in capsule

C5.title: The Treehouse Mystery
C5.concept: Friends find their treehouse has been used while they were away. Who's been here? Clues everywhere - someone's living in it! Turns out a stray cat had kittens inside. They help.
C5.character: The Treehouse Club - three friends who solve the mystery together
phonics_focus: Contractions: can't, won't, don't, we'll, they're
C5.visual_style: Mystery atmosphere, treehouse details, kitten cuteness reveal

C5.title: Everyone's Got Something
C5.concept: New kid at school doesn't think they're special. Classmates show their things - drawing, running, kindness. New kid realizes their something: they notice everyone else's gifts.
C5.character: Jamie (new kid) and diverse classmates with different talents
C5.theme: Everyone has value, the gift of seeing others
C5.story_arc: Feeling ordinary → seeing others → still feeling ordinary → realization
C5.visual_style: Classroom diversity, talent showcases, warm community

C5.title: We'll Get There
C5.concept: Family road trip goes wrong - flat tire, wrong turn, it's getting dark. Dad's stressed. Then they find an unexpected beautiful spot. Best accident ever.
C5.character: The Wilson family on their chaotic adventure
C5.theme: Happy accidents, going with the flow
C5.story_arc: Plans → disasters → frustration → unexpected beauty → gratitude
C5.visual_style: Road trip feel, stress to serenity, surprise vista reveal

C6.title: The Biggest Race
C6.concept: Tortoise and Hare story retold - this time Hare has learned. She trains hard, stays focused. But Tortoise has also trained! A real race. Both win in different ways.
C6.story_arc: Training → race day → close competition → both achieve personal goals
C6.visual_style: Sports montage style, determination faces, photo finish

C6.title: The Day Everything Changed
C6.concept: An ordinary Tuesday - kid walks to school, same old route. But today: notices a new friend, tries something new at lunch, speaks up in class. Same day, new experience.
C6.character: Eli, who decides to do things differently today
C6.setting: School day, same setting seen differently
C6.story_arc: Ordinary start → small brave choice → chain reaction → transformed day
C6.visual_style: Same settings with different energy, progressively brighter

C6.title: The Jumping Contest
C6.concept: Farm animals have a jumping contest. Each animal has a different style - horse jumped highest, frog jumped farthest, grasshopper jumped most times. Everyone's a winner.
C6.character: Farmyard friends competing in their own ways
C6.story_arc: Competition starts → different jumps → who won? → everyone won something
C6.visual_style: Sporting event, different jump styles, multiple podiums

C7.title: The Hopeless Garden
C7.concept: A girl inherits a hopeless, dead garden. Everyone says give up. She doesn't. Works tirelessly. One day, suddenly - a sprout! Then more. Garden becomes beautiful, hope restored.
C7.character: Grace, stubborn optimist with gardening gloves
C7.setting: Overgrown abandoned garden brought back to life
C7.story_arc: Inheritance → seeming hopelessness → daily work → first sign → transformation
C7.visual_style: Before/after transformation, patience montage, bloom explosion

C7.title: The Peaceful Kingdom
C7.concept: A kingdom where everyone's always fighting. New ruler says: 'Let's try kindness.' At first, nothing. Then slowly, change. Kingdom becomes peaceful, one act at a time.
C7.character: Young Queen Harmony and her skeptical but changing subjects
C7.story_arc: Conflict → new approach → doubt → small changes → transformation
C7.visual_style: Kingdom evolution, harsh to soft colors, community scenes

C7.title: The Fearless Kitten
C7.concept: Kitten is fearless (or so she thinks). Climbs too high, goes too far. Gets stuck. Learns that fearless doesn't mean careless. Bravery includes knowing limits.
C7.character: Daring the kitten, who learns the difference between brave and reckless
C7.setting: Home and neighborhood, increasingly precarious spots
C7.story_arc: Fearless acts → escalation → stuck → rescue → understanding
C7.visual_style: Kitten adventures, height tension, wise ending

C8.title: The Impossible Invention
C8.concept: Young inventor tries to build a flying machine. Fails repeatedly. Father says it's impossible. She doesn't stop. Redesigns, relearns. Final version... works! Father amazed.
C8.character: Iris, a relentless inventor who won't quit
phonics_focus: Prefixes: un-, re-, pre-, dis-, mis-
C8.visual_style: Workshop evolution, failed machines, triumphant flight

C8.title: The Unfair Race
C8.concept: A race where some runners get head starts. Main character thinks it's unfair - until she learns some runners have obstacles she can't see. Perspective shift.
C8.character: Maya, who learns about equity vs. equality
C8.story_arc: Confusion → complaint → explanation → understanding → supporting others
C8.visual_style: Race setup, invisible obstacles made visible, empathy moment

C8.title: Rewrite the Rules
C8.concept: Kids in a town follow outdated rules that don't make sense anymore. They propose rewriting them - respectfully. Adults listen. Town becomes better with updated rules.
C8.character: Council of kids who question and improve
C8.setting: Small town with silly old rules
C8.theme: Respectful questioning of tradition, positive change
C8.story_arc: Noticing problems → organizing → presenting case → compromise → improvement
C8.visual_style: Town hall meeting, before/after community scenes

D1.title: The Lighthouse Keeper
D1.concept: Old lighthouse keeper is retiring. New keeper arrives - young, different methods. They clash. Storm comes, they must work together. Mutual respect develops through crisis.
D1.character: Old keeper (Margaret, traditional) and new keeper (James, modern)
D1.story_arc: Tension → forced collaboration → crisis → mutual saving → understanding
D1.visual_style: Dramatic coastal setting, lighthouse detail, storm intensity

D1.title: The Unexpected Visitor
D1.concept: Family has a stranger knock on door during a storm. Should they let them in? They do. Stranger has amazing stories. Leaves a gift - a book that changes everything.
D1.character: The Chen family and a mysterious traveling storyteller
phonics_focus: Dialogue tags: asked, replied, whispered, shouted
D1.story_arc: Dilemma → kindness → stories shared → departure → lasting gift
D1.visual_style: Storm outside, warm inside, storytelling glow

D1.title: Two Languages, One Heart
D1.concept: Child translator helps grandmother who only speaks Spanish communicate with new neighbors. Realizes being bilingual is a superpower that connects worlds.
D1.character: Sofia, bridge between grandmother and community
D1.story_arc: Translation challenge → frustration → success → appreciation → pride
D1.visual_style: Two cultures blending, warmth of connection

D2.title: The Hidden Garden
D2.concept: Girl moves to old estate, finds a locked garden. Key is hidden somewhere in the house. As she searches, she learns about the garden's history and the family who left it behind.
D2.character: Lily, newcomer uncovering layers of history
D2.theme: Uncovering the past, new life from old
D2.story_arc: Move → discovery → search → history revelation → restoration begins
D2.visual_style: Gothic mystery atmosphere, before/after garden hints

D2.title: The Secret Society
D2.concept: Kids discover a secret club from 50 years ago. Find the old meeting place, the codes, the records. Realize the members were their grandparents. Restart the society.
D2.character: Four friends uncovering their grandparents' secret past
D2.setting: School, secret basement room, grandparents' homes
D2.visual_style: Mystery clues, old photographs, generational parallels

D2.title: What the Old Tree Knows
D2.concept: An ancient oak tree in town is scheduled to be cut down. Kids research its history - it's witnessed everything. They campaign to save it, learning about change and memory.
D2.character: Neighborhood kids and the 300-year-old oak tree
D2.setting: Town past and present, tree as witness
D2.visual_style: Tree through eras, historical flashbacks, community gathering

D3.title: The Architect's Secret
D3.concept: A young architect discovers blueprints for a building that was never built. Why? She investigates, finding the original architect had a vision too ahead of its time. She builds it now.
D3.character: Maya, young architect with connection to the past
D3.setting: Architecture firm, historical archives, construction site
phonics_focus: Latin roots: struct, dict, ject, port
D3.theme: Ideas ahead of their time, honoring visionaries
D3.story_arc: Discovery → research → understanding → modern adaptation → completion

D3.title: The Transport Mystery
D3.concept: Old train station has a mystery - trains used to disappear. New kid investigates, finds a hidden track, a secret route used during wartime to protect refugees.
phonics_focus: Latin roots: port, rupt, dict, ject
D3.visual_style: Train station atmosphere, historical mystery, heroic reveals

D3.title: Project: Time Capsule
D3.concept: Class creates a time capsule for 100 years from now. What do they include? Debates about what matters, what future people need to know. Reveals what kids value.
D3.character: Diverse classroom with different perspectives on importance
D3.theme: What matters, legacy, perspective on time
D3.visual_style: Classroom discussions, capsule items, future imagination

D4.title: Signals from Kepler
D4.concept: Young scientist detects unusual signals from exoplanet Kepler-442b. Is it natural? Or something else? The investigation requires biology, physics, and imagination.

phonics_focus: Greek roots: graph, phon, photo, bio, geo
D4.story_arc: Detection → investigation → hypothesis → testing → open-ended wonder
D4.visual_style: Space imagery, scientific equipment, data visualizations

D4.title: The Photographer's Journey
D4.concept: A photographer documents a dying language - the last speakers, their stories, their geography. Racing against time to preserve what's being lost.

D4.title: The Symphony of Science
D4.concept: A composer creates music using sounds from nature - whale songs, earthquake frequencies, solar wind data. Art and science merge into something beautiful and new.
D4.character: Composer who hears music in scientific data
D4.setting: Studio with scientific equipment, nature recordings
D4.theme: Science and art are connected, finding beauty in data
D4.visual_style: Sound waves, nature imagery, concert hall

D5.title: The Winter of Words
D5.concept: A writer is blocked, frozen. She retreats to a cabin in winter. The silence is terrifying, then healing. Words return, changed. She writes her best work from stillness.
D5.character: Author finding her voice again through silence
D5.theme: Creativity needs rest, silence has value
D5.story_arc: Block → escape → struggle with silence → acceptance → breakthrough
D5.visual_style: Winter isolation beauty, cabin intimacy, metaphor visuals

D5.title: The Storm Singer
D5.concept: A girl discovers she can sense storms before they come - she feels them as music. This gift helps her community but also sets her apart. Learning to live with extraordinary ability.
D5.character: Marina, who experiences weather as symphony
D5.setting: Coastal village dependent on weather knowledge
D5.theme: Gifts come with responsibility, being different
D5.story_arc: Discovery → doubt → acceptance → crisis → using gift → belonging
D5.visual_style: Synesthesia visuals, weather as music, emotional storms

D5.title: The Library of Lost Books
D5.concept: A library exists where books that were never finished are kept - authors who died, manuscripts that were lost. A librarian cares for them, sometimes finishing them herself.
D5.theme: Stories want to be finished, completion vs. perfection
D5.story_arc: Introduction to library → special book found → research → completion → release
D5.visual_style: Magical library, floating text, story imagery

D6.title: The Bridge Between
D6.concept: A teen moves between two worlds - their parents' traditional culture and their friends' modern one. A bridge builder, but exhausted. Eventually creates their own space that honors both.

D6.story_arc: Tension → exhaustion → crisis → integration → new identity
D6.visual_style: Two distinct visual worlds merging, bridge imagery

D6.title: The Last Summer
D6.concept: Friends know this summer is their last together before everyone scatters. They try to make it perfect but imperfections make it memorable. Bittersweet beauty of endings.
D6.character: Four friends facing the end of an era

D6.story_arc: Awareness of ending → trying too hard → disasters → acceptance → memory-making
D6.visual_style: Golden summer light, nostalgic moments, group dynamics

D6.title: The Letters We Never Sent
D6.concept: When grandmother dies, family finds box of unsent letters. Each family member reads one addressed to them. Secrets, apologies, love. Family heals through understanding her.
D6.character: Three generations processing a life through letters
D6.setting: Family home, grandmother's room, each reader's space
D6.story_arc: Death → discovery → reading → processing → family unity
